title: Minimal source-change re-fetch check (hash-diff) for provenance allow-list sources
context: The provenance allow-list pins each source with a SHA-256 snapshotHash. If a source's license or content changes after the snapshot, the project may unknowingly be using a now-incompatible source. A minimal hash-diff check — manually triggered in M0, automated in M1 (watcher-002) — re-fetches each allow-listed source URL and compares the content hash to the pinned value, flagging any drift for maintainer review. This keeps the supply chain auditable.
objective: Implement a minimal, manually-runnable script (scripts/check-sources.ts or similar) that reads data/provenance/allow-list.yaml, re-fetches each entry's canonical URL, computes the SHA-256 of the retrieved content, compares it to the stored snapshotHash, and prints a diff report (MATCH | CHANGED | UNREACHABLE per entry). Does not auto-update; flags only. Will be automated in watcher-002.
acceptanceCriteria: scripts/check-sources.ts (or .js) reads data/provenance/allow-list.yaml and, for each entry with a url and snapshotHash, fetches the URL and computes SHA-256 of the response body
Outputs a per-source report: MATCH (hash matches stored value), CHANGED (hash differs — prints both hashes), or UNREACHABLE (fetch failed — prints error)
Exits non-zero if any entry is CHANGED or UNREACHABLE, so a maintainer can spot drift
Script is runnable standalone (node scripts/check-sources.js or pnpm run check-sources) and documented in a brief README note
Does NOT auto-update allow-list.yaml; flags only — a human reviews and decides
pnpm build && pnpm lint passes; script added to package.json scripts as check-sources
resources: PLAN.md — Security & privacy (supply-chain; hash/archive snapshots; source-change watcher)
output: scripts/check-sources.ts (compiled) + entry in package.json scripts; brief usage note in CONTRIBUTING.md or a scripts/README.md
